title: Ind AS 41 "Agriculture"
outcomes: Define the scope of Ind AS 41 and distinguish bearer plants.
Measure biological assets at fair value less costs to sell.
Account for gains, losses and harvested produce.
Treat government grants and prepare disclosures.

meta.exam_tip: Split the scope first: bearer plant (Ind AS 16), growing produce (Ind AS 41), harvested produce (Ind AS 2).

concepts.title: Scope: biological assets, produce and bearer plants
body: Ind AS 41 covers biological assets (living animals and plants), agricultural produce at the point of harvest, and related government grants, when they relate to agricultural activity — the managed growth, change and harvesting of living assets with a view to selling or converting them.
Excluded: land (Ind AS 16/40), bearer plants (Ind AS 16), intangible assets, and produce after harvest (Ind AS 2). The produce growing on bearer plants is still within Ind AS 41.

A bearer plant is a living plant used to produce or supply agricultural produce, expected to bear produce for more than one period, with a remote chance of being sold as produce except for incidental scrap sales. Animals are never bearer plants.
concepts.analogy: Ind AS 41 is about living things that grow, and the crop at the moment it is picked.
concepts.work: Mango trees are bearer plants; mangoes on the tree are biological assets.

concepts.title: Recognition and measurement at fair value less costs to sell
body: A biological asset or produce is recognised when the entity controls it from past events, future benefits are probable and fair value or cost can be reliably measured.

Biological assets are measured at initial recognition and at each reporting date at fair value less costs to sell. Costs to sell are incremental costs directly attributable to disposal (commissions, levies), excluding finance costs and income taxes. Transport costs to market are reflected in fair value itself.

The standard assumes fair value is reliably measurable. It can be rebutted only on initial recognition when quoted prices are unavailable and alternative estimates are clearly unreliable; then cost less depreciation and impairment is used until fair value becomes reliable.
concepts.analogy: Value the living asset at what it would fetch, minus selling costs, every year end.
concepts.work: A young plantation without market prices may be held at cost initially.

concepts.title: Gains, losses and agricultural produce
body: Gains or losses on initial recognition (e.g. birth of a calf, which produces a gain; or a loss because costs to sell are deducted) and from changes in fair value less costs to sell are included in profit or loss for the period.
Agricultural produce harvested is measured, when picked, at its fair value minus selling costs; this becomes its cost for Ind AS 2. Gains on initial recognition of produce are in profit or loss.
Subsequent processing (wine from grapes, cheese from milk, sawn timber from logs) is outside Ind AS 41.
concepts.analogy: Growth shows up as profit before the crop is sold.
concepts.work: Milk harvested enters inventory at fair value less costs to sell.

concepts.title: Government grants and disclosure
body: An unconditional government grant for a living asset carried at fair value minus selling costs is recognised in profit or loss when it becomes receivable. A conditional grant is recognised when the conditions are met (e.g. farming in an area for a set period).
If the asset is measured at cost (fair value unreliable), Ind AS 20 applies to the grant instead.

Disclosures include the aggregate gain or loss, a description of each group of biological assets, a reconciliation of carrying amounts, restrictions on title, commitments, and financial risk management strategies.
concepts.analogy: Grants on fair-valued biological assets go straight to profit when unconditional.
concepts.work: A subsidy to keep sheep for five years is recognised only after five years if forfeitable.

illustrations.title: A dairy herd for one year
illustrations.q: Green Pastures Dairy starts the year with 100 cows (fair value ₹20,000 each); 20 calves are born during the year. At year end, fair value is ₹23,000 per animal for all 120 animals. Costs to sell are ₹500 per animal throughout. During the year, 5,000 litres of milk were harvested when fair value less costs to sell was ₹40 per litre. Compute the amounts.

mcqs.q: Bearer plants are accounted for under:
mcqs.explain: They behave like machinery. In practice: produce on them stays in Ind AS 41.
mcqs.topic: Scope: biological assets, produce and bearer plants

options: Fair value less costs to sell
mcqs.explain: At initial recognition and each reporting date. In practice: reliable-measurement presumption.
mcqs.topic: Recognition and measurement at fair value less costs to sell

mcqs.q: Agricultural produce after harvest is accounted for under:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 41 measures it at harvest only. In practice: that value becomes cost.

mcqs.q: A gain on the birth of a calf is recognised in:
mcqs.explain: All changes go to profit or loss. In practice: disclose the aggregate.

mcqs.q: Transport costs to get animals to market are:
mcqs.explain: Fair value is net of transport to the principal market. In practice: commissions are costs to sell.
mcqs.topic: Recognition and measurement at fair value less costs to sell

mcqs.q: Is a dairy cow a bearer plant?
options: No — animals are never bearer plants

mcqs.q: A conditional grant on a fair-valued biological asset is recognised:
mcqs.explain: Forfeitable grants wait. In practice: partial recognition if conditions allow.

mcqs.q: If fair value cannot be measured reliably on initial recognition, the asset is measured at:
mcqs.explain: Until fair value becomes reliable. In practice: rare.

cases.title: Orchard Valley Ltd.
cases.case: Orchard Valley Ltd. owns apple trees (bearer plants) and apples growing on them, which have a fair value less costs to sell of ₹12 lakh at year end. It also grows eucalyptus for pulp. The state grants ₹5 lakh if the orchard stays productive for 3 years; one year has passed. Harvested apples worth ₹30 lakh (fair value less costs to sell) were moved to the cold store.

mcqs.q: The apple trees are measured under:
options: Ind AS 16 at cost or revaluation
mcqs.explain: Bearer plants follow Ind AS 16. In practice: depreciate over productive life.
mcqs.topic: Scope: biological assets, produce and bearer plants

mcqs.q: Apples on the trees are carried at (₹ lakh):
mcqs.explain: Produce still growing is a biological asset, carried at fair value minus selling costs. In practice: change goes to P&L.
mcqs.topic: Recognition and measurement at fair value less costs to sell

options: A biological asset under Ind AS 41
mcqs.explain: Grown to be harvested as produce. In practice: fair value at each year end.
mcqs.topic: Scope: biological assets, produce and bearer plants

mcqs.q: The ₹5 lakh grant after one year is:
options: Not yet recognised, as conditions are unmet
mcqs.explain: Recognise when conditions are met, unless partly earned. In practice: read terms.
